answer: One defence is a stake-bonded reputation ledger: each agent locks a deposit — a pearl of value held in escrow — before it can trade. Honest work earns the deposit back with interest, but detected fraud burns it, so creating a hundred fake identities costs a hundred deposits. A violet flag marks identities whose behaviour diverges from their attested history, and every transaction leaves an echo in the public ledger that peers can audit. The cost of faking scales linearly while the benefit of one more identity stays flat, so sybil attacks stop paying for themselves.
